correctness.rationale: For a sector with j positive coordinates, integration against √m δ(sum y_i) gives mass density √m s^(m−2)/[(j−1)!(m−j−1)!] on 0≤s≤1/2. With multiplicity binom(m,j), the sum of the weights without √m equals binom(2m−2,m−1)/(m−2)! by Vandermonde. The weighted mean of 1/(j+1) equals (2m−1)/[m(m+1)], since dividing binom(m,j) by j+1 gives binom(m+1,j+1)/(m+1) and the second Vandermonde sum is binom(2m−1,m). The two independent simplex blocks and E(s²)=(m−1)/[4(m+1)] therefore give the claimed trace of B_m. Permutations make the covariance scalar on the zero-sum space. For k=n−m>0 the free block has norm radius Beta(k,m), by the shell density R^(k−1) times (1−R)^(m−1); the norm fractions of its k signed coordinates have Dirichlet(1,…,1) magnitudes. Its Beta second moments scale the two blocks exactly as claimed and independent sign symmetry kills the cross terms. The volume integral and the covariance reduce directly to the asserted ratio, also at k=0 by using B_m itself. Writing f_{m+1}/f_m=1+δ_m, the coefficient bound binom(m,j)≤m(m−1)^(j−1) gives a geometric majorant; 1−(m−1)δ_m=(2m²+1)/[(2m−1)(m+2)]>0. The positive margin displayed in RESULT.md exceeds that majorant and 1−r_m²=(3m−1)/(4m³)>0. These are proofs for every admissible m, not finite extrapolation. Replayed both margins and the denominator identity in `python3 /workspace/checks/independent_01_05.py` (check 2). The 1,058 checks in frozen VERIFICATION.md are recorded, not independently rerun.
